core.title: Give every non-draft WMBT at least one acceptance
core.given: A plan contains a WMBT whose status is not draft and that is not on the rule's allow-list of WMBTs without acceptances
core.when: WMBT acceptance coverage is checked or reviewed (any existing or new WMBT in the plan, regardless of what the current change touches)
core.then: The WMBT must have at least one acceptance criterion linked to it.
prefer: Write at least one acceptance for each WMBT in the same change that adds the WMBT or moves it out of draft.
Keep a WMBT in draft status until at least one acceptance exists for it.
avoid: Moving a WMBT out of draft before any acceptance exists for it.
Removing the last acceptance linked to a non-draft WMBT.
Attaching a placeholder or empty acceptance just to satisfy the count (gaming the metric).
Putting a WMBT on the rule's allow-list of WMBTs without acceptances, or setting it back to draft, just to silence the check.
unless: The WMBT is on the rule's allow-list of WMBTs without acceptances.
core.why: Acceptance coverage requires every non-draft WMBT to carry at least one acceptance; a WMBT without one has no acceptance to verify it against.
evidence: The coverage validator finds zero non-draft WMBTs without at least one linked acceptance, after excluding the WMBTs on the rule's allow-list of WMBTs without acceptances.
A reviewer confirms each non-draft, non-allow-listed WMBT in the plan links to at least one acceptance.
verification: For each WMBT in the plan (existing or new, not only changed ones): if its status is draft, skip; if its id is on the rule's allow-list of WMBTs without acceptances, skip; otherwise count the acceptances linked to it and flag the WMBT when the count is < 1 (threshold: at least one).
The scan covers every plan that declares WMBTs, whether or not the current change touches it; findings include pre-existing violations found during unrelated work.
Severity 3. Disposition: strict — the rule fails on every finding.
The check only counts linked acceptances; it does not judge acceptance quality, which is governed by other planner acceptance conventions.

fires: A plan contains a non-draft WMBT that is not on the rule's allow-list of WMBTs without acceptances and has no linked acceptance, including a pre-existing one discovered while doing unrelated work (code/test-only changes included).
Planner adds a non-draft WMBT that is not on the allow-list and attaches no acceptance.
Planner changes a WMBT that is not on the allow-list from draft to a non-draft status while it has no acceptance.
Planner deletes the last acceptance linked to a non-draft WMBT that is not on the allow-list.
The coverage check reports a non-draft WMBT with zero acceptances that is not on the allow-list.
doesNotFire: WMBT has draft status, even with no acceptance.
WMBT is on the rule's allow-list of WMBTs without acceptances, even with no acceptance.
Every non-draft, non-allow-listed WMBT in the plan already has at least one linked acceptance.

neutralityNotes: WMBT, wagon plan and acceptance are ATDD plan-model concepts (the closed vocabulary lists wmbt, acceptance, wagon as artifact params and plan-artifact kinds), so the core keeps them rather than degenerating to 'plan artifact'. 'Draft status' is plan-model semantics and stays in the core. The only realization-specific content is identifiers: the wmbts_without_acceptance allow-list name, the wmbt_without_acceptance finding id and the wmbt_acceptance_coverage glossary term id (all in bunOnly); the core refers to the allow-list generically and describes the check generically. The allow-list is rule-specific data, not a stack-wide profile fact, so no profile key is proposed for it. bun.json does not state where plan artifacts live or how an acceptance is linked to a WMBT; a target stack must supply those from existing vocabulary keys (roots.plan, layout.plan_item, roles.plan_artifact.kinds, urn.wmbt, urn.acceptance), so proposedKeys is empty. Severity 3 and strict disposition are kept in core.verification, not the profile. Audit fields (validator implementation ref, legacy ids, aliases) are not agent-facing items and are realization details.
